summary.headline: CleanMax H1 FY27 EBITDA rose 56% to INR1,047 crore, with Q2 EBITDA at INR553 crore and FY28 guidance of at least INR3,000 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported H1 FY27 EBITDA of INR1,047 crore (vs INR670 crore) and Q2 EBITDA of INR553 crore (vs INR386 crore), with PAT of about INR120 crore against INR19 crore a year earlier. Operational RE power sales capacity reached about 3.6 GW after roughly 600 MW of commissioning in H1, and contracted-under-execution capacity is 2.6 GW. Management reiterated at least 1,500 MW of capacity addition this fiscal and at least INR3,000 crore reported EBITDA in FY28. CRISIL upgraded the company to AA stable, and weighted average cost of debt fell to about 8.3%. Bikaner grid curtailment eased from 70% at commissioning to 26% in October, though it cost about 5% of H1 EBITDA.

segments.name: RE power sales
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 EBITDA about INR986 crore vs INR620 crore; segment EBITDA margin about 84% vs 83.5% in March 2026. Operational capacity about 3.6 GW, with 2.6 GW contracted under execution.

segments.name: RE services
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 EBITDA about INR60 crore vs INR52 crore, about 20% growth. About 830 MW of RE services capacity is operational.

guidance_outlook: At least 1,500 MW of new capacity addition in FY27, reiterated.
FY28 reported EBITDA of at least INR3,000 crore; at 5x net debt/EBITDA this implies net debt of INR15,000-16,000 crore.
Kopal: first bay (about 220 MW) expected to commission in Oct-Dec quarter; second bay (300 MW connection) expected around January, within FY27.
Planning assumption of 100 bps rise in repo rate, translating to about 50 bps on project borrowing cost (8.2% to 8.7%), still within the 8.75% modelled.
Bikaner curtailment ramp-up: about 70% ramp-up in October onward per management; grid timing for remaining substation and UP lines outside company control.
capex_capacity: Total RE power sales operational capacity about 3,600 MW; portfolio aggregate about 13,200 MW as of 30 Sep 2026 (about 7.8 GW 18 months earlier).
Evacuation received about 3,200 MW (about 1,100 MW 18 months ago); evacuation applied for about 2,800 MW as of 30 Sep 2026; applied for a further 2 GW CTU after 30 Sep.
Plants commissioned in H1 at about 95% of budgeted cost; last three fiscals within 95-97% of budget. Trailing 12-month commissioning about 1,400 MW per year.
Building plants in 10 states; 7 operational, 3 contracted and under execution. Annual capex above INR10,000 crore.

Gross block INR15,182 crore; CapWIP about INR6,700 crore. Debt: INR6,075 crore against assets operational over one year (EBITDA about INR717 crore in H1) and INR5,100 crore against under-construction assets/holding company.
demand_pricing: Total RE contracted power sales about 6.3 GW. Data and AI about 41-42% of volume; hyperscalers about 27-28% of 6,200 MW pipeline; company cites about 35% share of hyperscaler contracted volumes in India.
Repeat business about 85% of new PPAs in H1 FY27 (about 75% in FY25 and FY26); over 600 corporate customers; 95% of customers rated A or above, 83% AA/AAA or multinational.

Weighted average PPA tenure 23 years. Blended tariff about INR4 for capacity under execution (50% solar, 50% wind), vs about INR3.1 for SECI utility wind-solar; weighted average tariff 3.98 vs 4.04 earlier, attributed to solar/wind mix and FX on about 20% dollar-denominated contracts.
Contracting about 1,100-1,200 MW a year in STU plus rooftop segment (about 100 deals a year).
Management said solar module prices are factored into capex for volumes from calendar 2027; around 100-150 MW of DCR modules planned for Jan-Mar 2027 with orders not yet placed.

qa_highlights.question: Operating cash flow was negative about INR2 billion in H1; why did payable days fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a bulky wind turbine vendor payment was made after a loan drawdown, reducing capital creditors. Payable days fell from about 334 in FY26 to about 134; management said about 135 days (around 140 for turbines) is the normalised level.

qa_highlights.question: How do hyperscalers view CTU-connected projects and green attributes?
qa_highlights.answer: Hyperscalers prefer CTU-connected wind-solar hybrids, especially in South India. CTU capacity is sold out till September 2028. Buyers retain flexibility to use power directly or for attributes; tariffs are identical either way.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company entering BESS/storage?
qa_highlights.answer: Storage has begun with STU customers, including a farm being built, and contracts with more customers in Maharashtra. Management will not report BESS as a separate line until it reaches about 5-10% of P&L.

qa_highlights.question: Competition in group captive STU segment and hyperscaler right to win?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CTU capacity was reserved for hyperscalers, while STU group captive remains diversified. It cited a 35% share of contracted hyperscaler volumes in India and a demand-supply gap.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of a possible rate hike and tariff decline on project IRRs?
qa_highlights.answer: Over 50% of borrowings are fixed. Management planned for a 100 bps rise, which would lift project borrowing cost to about 8.7% vs 8.75% modelled, so equity IRR is unaffected, it said.

qa_highlights.question: Regulatory risk from daytime solar restrictions in Maharashtra?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a retrospective application of such a rule would hit fleet EBITDA by at most about 2%, and that this could be mitigated by reselling power to other customers.

risks_watch: Bikaner curtailment: 26% in October; timing of grid substation and UP line completion is outside company control.
Interest rate hardening: 46% of debt floating; rise in borrowing cost and dependence on FY28 leverage path.
Operating cash flow: negative in H1 due to capital creditor payments; payables normalisation to watch.
Tax outflow: about INR170 crore paid in H1 at holding company level, raised as a modelling question.
Hyperscaler deal timing is lumpy (roughly one announcement a year) and no pipeline guidance was given.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, execution and credit upgrade. More cautious on curtailment timing and deal timing, and deflected on pricing of module procurement and detailed PLF and tax modelling questions.
key_quotes: And a INR553 crores EBITDA for the quarter itself versus INR386 crores for the corresponding period last year.
We are delighted to see it at a low number of 26% in October.
We don't give guidance on customer contract signing, because very difficult for us to predict a precise point in time by which they will sell, they will contract.
So, even a 100 bps increase in RBI's repo rate leads us to have the same equity IRR we had always modeled.
